prompts.concept:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: game equipment approval concept sheet.
Create a polished 4 by 4 matrix of SIXTEEN DISTINCT full-body tactical armor outfit designs for a modern extraction game, worn on identical fully clothed short stylized mannequin bodies (3.5-head game proportions, neutral blank gray heads, relaxed arms, no weapons). Show each front three-quarter view large enough for silhouette, construction and dominant fabric colors to read. An art-director presentation on pale warm gray, crisp tailored cloth and readable simplified hard-surface panels; convincing stylized 3D game concept render, not photoreal. All bodies covered with practical opaque uniforms; no body or face redesign.
Four ROWS labeled C, B, A, S. Four COLUMNS labeled MOBILITY, BALANCED, HEAVY, MAINTENANCE. Every cell labeled C1 C2 C3 C4, B1 B2 B3 B4, A1 A2 A3 A4, S1 S2 S3 S4.
Row C: salvaged gear, dominant weathered olive and earth brown, rusty orange repairs, obvious patched fabric, mismatched reclaimed plates and improvised fasteners.
Row B: old civilian security/industrial gear, dominant dusty blue-gray uniforms with cream rounded shells, ochre safety details, visibly factory-made rounded equipment rather than military.
Row A: regular military, dominant deep dark olive and charcoal uniforms, brick red markings, precise angular modular armor, coherent issued equipment.
Row S: advanced expedition/special operations, dominant cobalt navy uniforms with porcelain white and silver armor panels and restrained cyan functional markings, engineered layered shells, no magical fantasy.
Columns must differ strongly in SILHOUETTE as well as color: MOBILITY compact chest carrier, flexible shoulders and small pouches; BALANCED standard symmetrical chest armor and moderate belt modules; HEAVY broad layered chest and separate shoulder panels, hip and shin protection with visible joint freedom; MAINTENANCE task harness, asymmetric service/tool modules, service backpack, instrument forearm and utility pouches, practical maintenance role. No enormous spikes or superhero armor. Heavy shoulder pieces must articulate away from shoulder joints. Keep neck, underarm, elbow and hip fitting regions clear for future Blender fitting. No helmets on heads in this board.
Title text: "EXTRACTION / ARMOR DESIGN DRAFT"
Small footer: "16 outfit concepts / approval required / not in game"
Clean exact matrix, consistent scale and camera, no cropped feet, generous spacing.
prompts.helmet:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a single polished production-oriented helmet design approval board for a modern stylized extraction game. Four rows C/B/A/S; 14 isolated helmet products total, front three-quarter product view, same scale, neutral gray background, no people, no heads. Title "EXTRACTION / HELMET DESIGN DRAFT". Strong readable shape differentiation, simplified durable materials suited to a game with large stylized heads; functional real-world-inspired armor without spikes, fantasy horns or enormous gear. Keep open rear/lower edges and clear neck articulation space for future character-specific original-color hair fitting. Every helmet an independent product compatible with mixed armor.
C row 3 products: C1 lightweight salvaged scout open helmet, C2 steel reinforced salvaged helmet, C3 repair worker helmet. Weathered olive brown cloth and rust orange salvaged plates, visibly repaired asymmetric construction.
B row 3: B1 rounded training lightweight helmet, B2 old civilian riot helmet with clear visor, B3 patrol field helmet. Dusty blue-gray shell, cream sections and ochre industrial safety accents.
A row 4: A1 military scout high-cut helmet, A2 regular military combat helmet, A3 SWAT face-protection helmet with short protective visor, A4 combat engineer service helmet. Dark olive/charcoal issued construction, brick red functional markings; angular modular but grounded military products.
S row 4: S1 special forces lightweight high-cut helmet, S2 special operations combat helmet, S3 juggernaut armored full face helmet, S4 expedition long-service modular helmet. Cobalt navy, porcelain white/silver plates and restrained cyan markers; clearly more refined, layered composite engineering than row B, no huge sci-fi antenna forests.
Readable labels C1 C2 C3 / B1 B2 B3 / A1 A2 A3 A4 / S1 S2 S3 S4. Do not invent a C4 or B4. Each row aligned generous spacing, no crops, small color swatches per row. Footer "14 helmet concepts / approval required / not in game". This is a concept board, not finished models or claims of protective stats.
prompts.subculture:
Edit the attached 16-cell armor concept board. Preserve EXACTLY the 4x4 row/column layout, all C1..S4 labels, product roles, dominant tier palettes and professional clean render quality. User correction: this is a SUBCULTURE ANIME EXTRACTION GAME; existing all-covered uniforms are the wrong direction. Redesign the outfits as stylish female anime tactical costumes on visibly ADULT (age 25+) faceless female fashion mannequins, neutral relaxed poses. Nonsexual professional costume design sheet.
Maintain deliberate skin exposure in each outfit, with varied bare upper arms/shoulders, exposed midriff/side waist, and upper thighs above stockings or leg armor. Use secure opaque cropped tactical tops, fitted shorts or short practical skirts over opaque shorts, thigh straps and separated knee/shin armor. Chest/buttocks/pelvis fully covered, no lingerie, no bikini, no cleavage focus, no erotic poses. Body coverage may increase for HEAVY, but do not turn all designs back into full jumpsuits. Every role needs at least one clearly open region (arm, waist or thigh).
MOBILITY: compact cropped carrier, sleeveless arms, utility shorts and lightweight thigh straps.
BALANCED: structured opaque cropped top/vest, one or both shoulders open, protected waist belt with visible abdominal gap and short tactical skirt/shorts.
HEAVY: broad chest and floating shoulder plates, armored shorts and separate knee/shin modules; open joints and some thigh/upper arm visible rather than a sealed suit.
MAINTENANCE: short work jacket or cropped service vest with rolled sleeves, asymmetric tool harness and practical utility shorts; no medical/healing symbols.
C salvaged olive/brown/rust, B dusty blue gray/cream/ochre rounded civilian equipment, A dark olive/charcoal/brick red military, S navy/cobalt/porcelain white/cyan advanced. Improve feminine subculture costume silhouettes without changing into fantasy armor or changing faces/hair (mannequins have no features/hair).
Keep title "EXTRACTION / ARMOR DESIGN DRAFT", labels and footer. This is an APPROVAL CONCEPT, not fitted 3D. Clear functional attachment points for future fitting.
prompts.fitted:
Use case: identity-preserve / costume design.
Create an eight-character equipment approval concept sheet using the TWO supplied game character renders as strict identity AND BODY PROPORTION references. Image1 brown-haired SERIN, image2 pale-lavender-haired EDEL. These are stylized SD game characters: huge heads, short limbs, compact bodies. DO NOT turn them into tall adult fashion models or normalize their different torso shapes. Maintain the original faces, eyes, hair colors and recognizable hairstyles. Remove all guns from the reference poses, set both arms relaxed slightly away from torso, full bodies with feet visible. Add nonsexual practical tactical game clothing over their basewear, with secure opaque tops and shorts; no underwear visible, no cleavage emphasis, no sexual posing.
Layout: four columns C / B / A / S, two rows: EDEL upper row and SERIN lower row. Each column shows the SAME armor product adapted to each character, with separately fitted torso curvature, shoulder width, belt height and thigh straps. Large crisp figures and generous spacing on neutral gray. Exact same character proportions in all columns.
User wants a SUBCULTURE tactical game costume direction retaining some exposed regions, rather than full-body jumpsuits. Keep bare upper arms/shoulders, a modest gap of abdomen between short armored vest and waistband, and some upper thigh above knee pads. Fully cover chest, buttocks and pelvis. Avoid bikini/lingerie. Use short utility shorts or a short tactical skirt over shorts, gloves and practical boots. These are outfit design concepts, not claims of actual Blender fitting.
C: explorer light outfit, dominant salvaged olive and earth brown with rust orange repair patches, thin asymmetric reclaimed chest plates, utility straps.
B: patrol balanced outfit, dominant dusty blue-gray cropped security vest with cream rounded chest plates and ochre markers, neat civilian industrial silhouette.
A: regular military balanced outfit, dominant dark olive/charcoal opaque cropped armored vest with brick red small markings, angular plate carrier, separate narrow shoulder modules and belt pouches.
S: special operation balanced outfit, cobalt navy opaque top and shorts with porcelain white/silver layered plates and restrained cyan markers, compact refined engineering with open arm joints.
Protect the original hair silhouette and hair color; no helmets in this sheet. Equipment must sit over the body naturally without oversized shoulders crushing the neck. Use stylized 3D game render shading matching the references, not realistic humans.
Title: "EDEL / SERIN — PROPORTION-MATCHED COSTUME DRAFT"
Column labels "C / SALVAGE", "B / PATROL", "A / MILITARY", "S / SPECIAL".
Footer "Design concept only / character-specific Blender fitting after approval".
prompts.tier:
Edit this EDEL/SERIN 8-character costume sheet. Keep the exact character identities, existing SD proportions, original hair colors/hairstyles, two rows and four columns, relaxed poses and skin exposure. This revision must demonstrate ONE SAME ARMOR ROLE ("BALANCED") across C/B/A/S tiers, with visibly different equipment GEOMETRY rather than palette swaps. Nonsexual practical subculture tactical costumes, opaque chest and shorts, no underwear visible, bare arms, modest midriff gap and some upper thigh remain. Do not elongate bodies.
Redesign the STRUCTURAL SHAPES:
C BALANCED: short patched cloth carrier with an irregular reclaimed trapezoid central steel plate plus a separate mismatched small side plate, diagonal exposed webbing, one coarse external fastening, uneven cloth hem. Thin scrappy and asymmetric, dominant brown/olive and rusty repaired edges.
B BALANCED: old civilian patrol vest with ONE continuous broad smooth rounded cream shield panel, blue-gray fabric bolsters, two large visible side release buckles. Rounded clean industrial design, no segmented military grids. Ochre safety accents.
A BALANCED: military modular carrier with THREE clearly angular fitted plate sections (central upper trapezoid and two lower quadrilateral sections), compact MOLLE pouch row, a distinct red quick-release pull tab, small separate angular shoulder straps. Dominant dark olive and charcoal. Precise issued angular engineering.
S BALANCED: specialized composite harness with FOUR slim overlapping swept beveled shell segments arranged as an articulated layered structure and a narrow central dark spine seam; suspended small side-rib panels, recessed attachment sockets and integrated cyan status detail. Predominantly navy with porcelain/silver shells. Clearly different outline and plate segmentation from B's single rounded shield and A's blocky grid; no superhero magical V chest or huge armor.
Each same product must visibly match between Edel and Serin rows, fitted to each character's torso separately. Product identities consistent between both.
Shorts/skirts, pouches, leg straps, knee pads, boots also structurally different by tier: C visibly repaired mismatched pads, B broad rounded shells, A angular standard-issue blocks, S thin layered composite plates. Keep comparable BALANCED bulk and the SAME functional role at all tiers; do not use progressively heavier/full-cover costumes as a substitute for actual tier shape design.
Title "BALANCED ARMOR / SAME ROLE, FOUR DISTINCT TIERS".
Columns "C / SALVAGED", "B / PATROL", "A / MILITARY", "S / COMPOSITE".
Footer "Concept only / Edel and Serin proportions / Blender fitting after approval".
Make the form differences immediately readable even if viewed in grayscale. Large figures, no tiny illegible annotations.
